answers.explanation: A pulse of light is a 1, no light is a 0.
When light hits the cladding at a shallow angle, it reflects back into the core.
The cladding bends light slightly less than the core, which is what makes total internal reflection work.
Light isn't affected by electrical noise, and light in one fiber doesn't leak into another.
Fiber is immune to electrical interference, so noise from power lines doesn't affect it.
Single-mode fiber has one light path, so pulses don't smear together over long distances.
In multimode fiber, light takes many paths and pulses smear together, which limits it to a few hundred meters. Long links use single-mode.
Fiber's weaknesses are cost and handling, not performance.
The last stretch to your home decides a lot, like whether upload speeds can match download.
Broadband coax is a shared medium. Everyone on the segment shares its capacity.
